sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the early 1950s, Sam Moore and his family left rural Arkansas, looking to start a new life.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代初，萨姆·摩尔和他的家人离开了阿肯色州的农村，想要开启新的生活。

sentences.en: They planned on moving to Chicago.
sentences.zh: 他们计划搬到芝加哥。

sentences.en: We were on our way to Chicago with all our worldly possessions and our dog's spot.
sentences.zh: 我们带着所有的家当和我们的狗“点点”在去芝加哥的路上。

sentences.en: And we started off in my granddaddy's 53 Dynaflo Buick and got to St. Louis and ran out of gas.
sentences.zh: 我们开着我爷爷那辆53年的别克Dynaflo出发，到了圣路易斯时没油了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And instead of continuing on to Illinois, Moore's family just decided to stay.
sentences.zh: 摩尔一家没有继续前往伊利诺伊州，而是决定留下来。

sentences.en: They settled in a middle-class area called The Ville.
sentences.zh: 他们在圣路易斯一个叫“维尔”（The Ville）的中产阶级社区定居了下来。

sentences.en: Back then, St. Louis was segregated, and The Ville was one of the only African-American neighborhoods in the city.
sentences.zh: 那时，圣路易斯实行种族隔离，而“维尔”是城里仅有的几个非裔美国人社区之一。

sentences.en: But residents of The Ville made the best of it.
sentences.zh: 但“维尔”的居民们还是尽量让生活过得好一些。

sentences.en: That's reporter Zach Dyer.
sentences.zh: 这是记者扎克·戴尔。

sentences.en: Black-owned businesses thrived, and the neighborhood became one of the most prosperous African-American communities in the country.
sentences.zh: 黑人经营的企业蓬勃发展，该社区成为了全国最繁荣的非裔美国人社区之一。

sentences.en: Do you mind if we just roll the windows up just for the recording?
sentences.zh: 你介意我们为了录音把车窗摇上去吗？

sentences.en: Okay, I'll turn the arrow on.
sentences.zh: 好的，我把转向灯打开。

sentences.en: Sam Moore's dad got a job as a bricklayer and helped build some of the beautiful, stately brick homes in this area.
sentences.zh: 萨姆·摩尔的父亲找了一份泥瓦匠的工作，参与建造了这个地区一些漂亮、庄严的砖房。

sentences.en: He was a great bricklayer.
sentences.zh: 他是一位出色的泥瓦匠。

sentences.en: He did quite a few jobs around this town.
sentences.zh: 他在这个镇上做过不少工程。

sentences.en: I still see some of my dad's work.
sentences.zh: 我至今还能看到一些我父亲的作品。

sentences.en: Oh, wow, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，哇，真的吗？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Beautiful homes, triple brick, three-story, two-story buildings.
sentences.zh: 漂亮的房子，三层砖墙，三层楼，两层楼的建筑。

sentences.en: That would cost a million dollars to duplicate.
sentences.zh: 如果要复制这些建筑，得花上一百万美元。

sentences.en: But driving around The Ville today, where Moore has lived for almost his entire life and is now the alderman, the neighborhood looks very different.
sentences.zh: 但今天开车在“维尔”转转——摩尔几乎一生都住在这里，现在是这里的议员——你会发现这个社区看起来大不相同。

sentences.en: We pull up in front of a couple of the old houses.
sentences.zh: 我们把车停在几栋老房子前。

sentences.en: Hold on one second.
sentences.zh: 等一下。

sentences.en: Look at these two buildings.
sentences.zh: 看看这两栋建筑。

sentences.en: Look at that building.
sentences.zh: 看看那栋建筑。

sentences.en: You can see clean through it.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接看穿它。

sentences.en: From the street, the building's facade looks normal.
sentences.zh: 从街上看，这栋建筑的立面看起来很正常。

sentences.en: It's a two-story brick home sitting on a white limestone base.
sentences.zh: 这是一栋坐落在白色石灰岩基座上的两层砖房。

sentences.en: Rounded brick arches frame the first floor windows.
sentences.zh: 圆形的砖拱门框住了二楼的窗户。

sentences.en: But head just around the corner and you can see that the entire sidewall is missing.
sentences.zh: 但转到拐角处，你会发现整面侧墙都不见了。

sentences.en: The bricks are just gone.
sentences.zh: 砖块完全消失了。

sentences.en: You can see straight into the rooms, each with a different wallpaper.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接看到里面的房间，每个房间都贴着不同的壁纸。

sentences.en: We call them dollhouses because you can look inside of them and see what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们称它们为“玩偶屋”，因为你可以往里看，看到里面是什么样。

sentences.en: Remember when the little girls played with the dollhouses, put the furniture in, you could see it, and you could put your hand in the wall.
sentences.zh: 还记得小女孩们玩玩偶屋的时候吗？把家具放进去，你能看到里面，还能把手伸进墙里。

sentences.en: In the past 50 years, the city of St. Louis has lost more than half its population.
sentences.zh: 在过去的50年里，圣路易斯市流失了超过一半的人口。

sentences.en: Vacancy has skyrocketed in The Ville and other neighborhoods on the north side.
sentences.zh: “维尔”和北部的其他社区，空置率直线上升。

sentences.en: Entire neighborhoods here are just green pasture, punctuated by the occasional dilapidated building that's slowly surrendering to the landscape around it.
sentences.zh: 这里的整个社区只剩下绿草地，偶尔点缀着几栋破败的建筑，正慢慢向周围的景观屈服。

sentences.en: When Moore became an alderman back in 2007, he started to get calls from his constituents complaining about these collapsing buildings.
sentences.zh: 摩尔在2007年当选议员后，开始接到选民的电话，投诉这些正在倒塌的建筑。

sentences.en: So he set out to discover why they were falling down.
sentences.zh: 于是他着手调查它们倒塌的原因。

sentences.en: He figured it was probably just because they were so old.
sentences.zh: 他原以为可能只是因为它们太老了。

sentences.en: But then he noticed that something was strange about these so-called dollhouses.
sentences.zh: 但后来他注意到这些所谓的“玩偶屋”有些奇怪。

sentences.en: They were surrounded by piles of broken bricks and debris, but something was missing.
sentences.zh: 它们周围堆满了碎砖和瓦砾，但少了点什么。

sentences.en: I often wondered why.
sentences.zh: 我经常纳闷为什么。

sentences.en: I never saw whole bricks.
sentences.zh: 我从来没见过完整的砖块。

sentences.en: If the buildings were falling down into piles, but there weren't any whole bricks in those piles, Moore knew it meant someone was taking them.
sentences.zh: 如果建筑倒塌成堆，但堆里没有完整的砖块，摩尔知道这意味着有人把它们拿走了。

sentences.en: Salvaged bricks are valuable.
sentences.zh: 回收的砖块很有价值。

sentences.en: There's a market for them, just like there's a market for the copper that gets stripped out of old homes.
sentences.zh: 它们有市场，就像从老房子里拆出来的铜线有市场一样。

sentences.en: A pickup truck full of old bricks could be worth upwards of $300.
sentences.zh: 一辆装满旧砖的皮卡车价值可能超过300美元。

sentences.en: But these bricks weren't being salvaged legally.
sentences.zh: 但这些砖并不是合法回收的。

sentences.en: Those were not legal demolition projects.
sentences.zh: 那些不是合法的拆迁项目。

sentences.en: They were theft.
sentences.zh: 那是盗窃。

sentences.en: It was brick theft.
sentences.zh: 那是砖块盗窃。

sentences.en: And this theft was happening on a massive scale in Moore's district.
sentences.zh: 这种盗窃在摩尔的选区大规模发生。

sentences.en: Well, I have 1,242 empty buildings and 1,700 vacant lots.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我有1242栋空置建筑和1700块空地。

sentences.en: So out of the 1,700 vacant lots, I guarantee you that 1,200 of them were stolen.
sentences.zh: 所以在那1700块空地里，我敢保证有1200块是被偷走的。

sentences.en: And despite these being vacant houses, all of this brick theft is a problem.
sentences.zh: 尽管这些都是空房子，但所有的砖块盗窃都是个问题。

sentences.en: When a building's bricks get stolen, the house usually can't be resold.
sentences.zh: 当一栋建筑的砖块被偷走后，房子通常就无法再转售了。

sentences.en: It also takes money out of the pockets of legal demolition workers.
sentences.zh: 这也从合法的拆迁工人手中抢走了钱。

sentences.en: And it stalls redevelopment because you can't sell a building when you can't guarantee that it'll be there next week.
sentences.zh: 而且它阻碍了重建，因为如果你不能保证一栋建筑下周还在那里，你就没法卖掉它。

sentences.en: But there's also something intangible that's lost with brick theft.
sentences.zh: 但砖块盗窃还导致了一些无形东西的流失。

sentences.en: The villa's been home to famous African Americans like Chuck Berry, Tina Turner, and the opera singer Grace Bunbury.
sentences.zh: “维尔”曾是查克·贝里、蒂娜·特纳和歌剧演员格蕾丝·邦伯里等著名非裔美国人的家园。

sentences.en: I remember the Grace Bunbury house.
sentences.zh: 我记得格蕾丝·邦伯里的房子。

sentences.en: That house was stole.
sentences.zh: 那房子被偷了。

sentences.en: And they just called them old raggedy buildings.
sentences.zh: 他们只是称它们为破旧的老建筑。

sentences.en: But a lot of our history was taken away and stole as well.
sentences.zh: 但我们的许多历史也被拿走和偷走了。

sentences.en: Brick theft has been going on all across St. Louis since at least the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 至少从20世纪70年代开始，砖块盗窃就在整个圣路易斯持续发生。

sentences.en: Whole buildings, whole blocks, whole parts of neighborhoods being stolen, carted off illegally, and sold.
sentences.zh: 整栋建筑、整个街区、整个社区的部分区域被偷走、非法运走并出售。

sentences.en: How and where in the United States can somebody steal a whole building and not get caught?
sentences.zh: 在美国，一个人怎么可能偷走整栋建筑而不被抓到？

sentences.en: St. Louis' history with bricks starts back in 1849, when a boat fire on the riverfront jumped into the city.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯的砖块历史始于1849年，当时河滨的一场船火蔓延到了城市。

sentences.en: Hundreds of wooden buildings along the river burned to the ground.
sentences.zh: 河边数百栋木制建筑被烧毁。

sentences.en: The fire's devastation led the city government to order that all new buildings be constructed with fireproof materials.
sentences.zh: 火灾的破坏促使市政府下令所有新建筑必须使用防火材料建造。

sentences.en: Luckily, the city happened to be sitting on top of a lot of high-quality clay,
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，这座城市恰好坐落在大量优质粘土之上，

sentences.en: as well as the coal that would be needed to fire the kilns to turn that clay into brick.
sentences.zh: 以及将粘土烧制成砖所需的煤炭。

sentences.en: Well, I could show you a couple of these different kinds of bricks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我可以给你看几种不同类型的砖。

sentences.en: Yeah, definitely.
sentences.zh: 好的，没问题。

sentences.en: One thing that I think is interesting is...
sentences.zh: 有一件事我觉得很有趣……

sentences.en: Andrew Weil is the executive director of the Landmarks Association of St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁·威尔是圣路易斯地标协会的执行董事。

sentences.en: Behind his desk, he's got a giant-framed pictorial map of the city back in the late 1800s.
sentences.zh: 在他办公桌后面，挂着一张19世纪末该市的巨幅画报地图。

sentences.en: The landscape is dotted with evidence of the city's once-thriving brick industry.
sentences.zh: 景观中点缀着这座城市曾经繁荣的砖业的证据。

sentences.en: It's covered with mines and smokestacks.
sentences.zh: 到处都是矿井和烟囱。

sentences.en: You'll see some smokestacks, and you'll see, you know, some sort of derricks set up,
sentences.zh: 你会看到一些烟囱，还会看到，你知道，某种架设起来的井架，

sentences.en: or winches set up over mines, some pit mines.
sentences.zh: 或者架在矿井上的绞车，一些露天矿。

sentences.en: And you'll also see these beehive kilns.
sentences.zh: 你还会看到这些蜂巢窑。

sentences.en: They look like big igloos.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来像巨大的冰屋。

sentences.en: The red clay industry was so big that folks were even digging mines in their backyards to get this stuff.
sentences.zh: 红粘土工业规模如此之大，以至于人们甚至在后院挖矿来获取这种材料。

sentences.en: And all this new industry attracted others to St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 所有这些新兴工业吸引了其他人来到圣路易斯。

sentences.en: In the decades to come, waves of migrants from across Europe and the southern U.S.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，来自欧洲和美国南部的移民潮

sentences.en: flocked to the city.
sentences.zh: 涌向这座城市。

sentences.en: It was a boomtown.
sentences.zh: 这是一个繁荣的城市。

sentences.en: So it's sort of a perfect storm of materials, labor, and industrial innovation
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种材料、劳动力和工业创新的完美结合，

sentences.en: that combine to make St. Louis into this brick-producing powerhouse.
sentences.zh: 共同将圣路易斯打造成了一个砖块生产强国。

sentences.en: By 1890, St. Louis was home to the world's largest brick manufacturing company.
sentences.zh: 到1890年，圣路易斯拥有了世界上最大的砖块制造公司。

sentences.en: Millions of bricks were exported across the country to build skyscrapers in Chicago
sentences.zh: 数以百万计的砖块被出口到全国各地，用于建造芝加哥的摩天大楼

sentences.en: and other buildings across the western and southern United States.
sentences.zh: 以及美国西部和南部的其他建筑。

sentences.en: Bricks were cheap and plentiful.
sentences.zh: 砖块既便宜又充足。

sentences.en: And that meant that even modest working-class homes in St. Louis could have one-of-a-kind brickwork.
sentences.zh: 这意味着即使是圣路易斯普通的工人阶级住宅，也能拥有独一无二的砖砌工艺。

sentences.en: They're not just blank facades.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅仅是空白的立面。

sentences.en: They have this sort of corbeling or extensions or recesses and ornamental bricks built into them,
sentences.zh: 它们有这种叠涩、延伸、凹槽和装饰砖，

sentences.en: pressed flowers or designs and string courses and things like that.
sentences.zh: 压制的花朵或图案、腰线之类的东西。

sentences.en: But even as these beautiful brick homes were going up all across the city,
sentences.zh: 但就在这些美丽的砖房在全市拔地而起的同时，

sentences.en: the conditions for the city's eventual semi-abandonment were also being put into place.
sentences.zh: 这座城市最终走向半荒废的条件也已经具备。

sentences.en: In the early 1900s, St. Louis was forcing its black citizens to live in segregated neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初，圣路易斯强迫黑人公民居住在种族隔离的社区。

sentences.en: When the practice was found unconstitutional,
sentences.zh: 当这种做法被裁定违宪时，

sentences.en: realtors began asking homeowners in St. Louis to sign something called race-restrictive deed covenants.
sentences.zh: 房地产经纪人开始要求圣路易斯的房主签署所谓的“种族限制契约”。

sentences.en: These barred the homeowner and future homeowners
sentences.zh: 这些契约禁止房主及未来的房主

sentences.en: from selling the property to African Americans and other minority groups.
sentences.zh: 将房产出售给非裔美国人和其他少数群体。

sentences.en: Here's Colin Gordon, a history professor at the University of Iowa.
sentences.zh: 这是爱荷华大学的历史学教授科林·戈登。

sentences.en: When realtors assessed properties for sale in St. Louis, you know, well into the 1960s,
sentences.zh: 当房地产经纪人评估圣路易斯的待售房产时，你知道，一直到20世纪60年代，

sentences.en: one of the standard items on the assessment form was the nearest Negro community
sentences.zh: 评估表上的标准项目之一就是最近的黑人社区，

sentences.en: or the degree to which Negroes had invaded or intruded upon a neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 或者黑人入侵或闯入一个社区的程度。

sentences.en: And is invasion a word that was used in these documents?
sentences.zh: “入侵”是这些文件中使用的词吗？

sentences.en: Oh yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的，是的。

sentences.en: These were the words that were used.
sentences.zh: 这些就是当时使用的词。

sentences.en: Intrusion, invasion, and the like.
sentences.zh: 闯入、入侵等等。

sentences.en: Not only were African Americans blocked from certain neighborhoods by these racist deed covenants,
sentences.zh: 非裔美国人不仅被这些种族主义契约挡在某些社区之外，

sentences.en: the city was also bulldozing black neighborhoods for massive new projects like the Gateway Arch.
sentences.zh: 市政府还在为像大拱门这样的大型新项目推平黑人社区。

sentences.en: This was the age of urban renewal.
sentences.zh: 这是城市更新的时代。

sentences.en: Increasingly, we are seeing large-scale demolition as the first step in building modern cities.
sentences.zh: 我们越来越多地看到大规模拆迁成为建设现代城市的第一步。

sentences.en: In this jet age, events move fast, faster indeed than we sometimes realize.
sentences.zh: 在这个喷气时代，事件发展迅速，确实比我们有时意识到的还要快。

sentences.en: And our progress is certain to be steady as we clear away the structures that block progress.
sentences.zh: 只要我们清除掉阻碍进步的结构，我们的进步就一定会稳步推进。

sentences.en: In the 1950s, white residents had started to leave the city entirely.
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代，白人居民开始完全离开这座城市。

sentences.en: The departure was facilitated by the recent development of the highway system and by the GI Bill,
sentences.zh: 这种离开得益于高速公路系统的最新发展和《退伍军人权利法案》，

sentences.en: which gave white veterans easy access to home loans while largely denying black veterans the same right.
sentences.zh: 该法案让白人退伍军人可以轻松获得住房贷款，而很大程度上拒绝了黑人退伍军人同样的权利。

sentences.en: White flight was happening all over the country.
sentences.zh: “白人逃离”现象在全国各地都在发生。

sentences.en: And St. Louis was no exception.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯也不例外。

sentences.en: As whites rushed to the suburbs, the city's population declined and its tax revenues plummeted.
sentences.zh: 随着白人涌向郊区，城市人口减少，税收收入暴跌。

sentences.en: By the 1970s, African Americans with the means started moving out of the city, too.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪70年代，有经济能力的非裔美国人也开始搬离城市。

sentences.en: We lost over a half a million people in this city since 1950.
sentences.zh: 自1950年以来，我们这座城市流失了超过五十万人。

sentences.en: So we have a huge problem with vacancy.
sentences.zh: 所以我们面临着巨大的空置问题。

sentences.en: Andrew Weil again from the Landmarks Association.
sentences.zh: 再次请出地标协会的安德鲁·威尔。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the neighborhoods that are vacant were built of incredibly high-quality materials and incredibly durable materials.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这些空置的社区是用极其优质和极其耐用的材料建造的。

sentences.en: Most of the brick that's being stolen in St. Louis is, you know, 100 or 120 years old.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯被偷走的大多数砖块，你知道，都有100或120年的历史了。

sentences.en: So it's really at the beginning of its lifespan.
sentences.zh: 所以它们实际上才刚刚进入寿命的初期。

sentences.en: Bricks can last for hundreds of years.
sentences.zh: 砖块可以使用几百年。

sentences.en: The fallout from decades of racist housing policies and disinvestment in the North Side
sentences.zh: 几十年来种族主义住房政策和对北区投资不足的后果，

sentences.en: has created communities where the bricks themselves are worth more than the homes they support.
sentences.zh: 创造了这样一个社区：砖块本身的价值比它们支撑的房屋还要高。

sentences.en: The only reason these buildings can be stolen is because they are perceived to have no value.
sentences.zh: 这些建筑之所以能被偷，唯一的原因就是人们认为它们没有价值。

sentences.en: So if the building is perceived to have no value and there aren't eyes watching it, you know, it's a perfect opportunity for it to disappear.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果人们认为这栋建筑没有价值，又没有人盯着它，你知道，它消失的机会就完美了。

sentences.en: By the time Sam Moore had become alderman in 2007, brick theft had already been going on for decades.
sentences.zh: 到萨姆·摩尔2007年成为议员时，砖块盗窃已经持续了几十年。

sentences.en: But there hadn't been much of an effort by the city to stop it.
sentences.zh: 但市政府并没有做出多大努力来阻止它。

sentences.en: So Moore set out to figure out who was stealing bricks and how.
sentences.zh: 于是摩尔着手调查是谁在偷砖以及如何偷的。

sentences.en: To start, he did what any gumshoe would do.
sentences.zh: 首先，他做了任何私家侦探都会做的事。

sentences.en: He went on some stakeouts.
sentences.zh: 他去蹲点守候。

sentences.en: I watched them steal the bricks and followed them to the brickyard where they sold them
sentences.zh: 我看着他们偷砖，并跟踪他们到卖砖的砖厂，

sentences.en: and wondered why would the city let an illegal organization like that or a business buy a brick?
sentences.zh: 我很纳闷，为什么市政府会允许像那样的非法组织或企业购买砖块？

sentences.en: These brick thieves have found that abandoned houses represent remarkably easy targets.
sentences.zh: 这些偷砖贼发现，废弃的房屋是极其容易下手的目标。

sentences.en: So easy that sometimes people are coming in from as far away as Las Vegas to steal them.
sentences.zh: 太容易了，以至于有时人们甚至远从拉斯维加斯赶来偷砖。

sentences.en: It's not actually hard to tear the buildings down.
sentences.zh: 其实拆除建筑并不难。

sentences.en: People go about it in a few different ways.
sentences.zh: 人们有几种不同的方法。

sentences.en: So the guy get up at 6 o'clock in the morning.
sentences.zh: 比如有人早上六点起床。

sentences.en: And get on a bicycle and take a screwdriver and pick him out six or seven bricks out of the wall and then snatch the wall.
sentences.zh: 骑上自行车，带把螺丝刀，从墙上抠下六七块砖，然后把墙拽倒。

sentences.en: That's all it takes is make a hole in the wall, slide a metal pipe in the hole, attach it to a chain,
sentences.zh: 只需要在墙上凿个洞，塞进一根金属管，系上一条链子，

sentences.en: give yourself enough clearance, and pull.
sentences.zh: 留出足够的空间，然后一拉。

sentences.en: Instant demolition.
sentences.zh: 瞬间拆除。

sentences.en: The thieves had figured out how to steal bricks even in busy areas.
sentences.zh: 小偷们甚至摸索出了如何在繁忙地段偷砖的方法。

sentences.en: They'd just take out the back wall of the house, hidden from view.
sentences.zh: 他们会把房子的后墙拆掉，避开视线。

sentences.en: Like this is a busy street.
sentences.zh: 比如这条街就很繁忙。

sentences.en: So what they did was they took the back out of this one.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做的是把这一栋的后墙拆了。

sentences.en: Look to your right.
sentences.zh: 往右看。

sentences.en: Oh, I see now.
sentences.zh: 哦，我看到了。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: So literally like the whole building is, the back of the building is gone and there's a tree that's grown up in it.
sentences.zh: 整栋建筑的后半部分确实都没了，里面还长出了一棵树。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But you're right, the whole building is just, there's nothing there in the back.
sentences.zh: 但你是对的，整栋建筑就是……后面什么都没有了。

sentences.en: There are various ways to steal an entire wall of brick.
sentences.zh: 偷走整面砖墙的方法有很多种。

sentences.en: Some people run a cable through one window and out another, then attach it to a truck and pull.
sentences.zh: 有些人会把缆绳穿过窗户，再从另一扇窗户拉出来，系在卡车上用力拉。

sentences.en: Or they've used backhoes that were contracted for other legal demolition jobs.
sentences.zh: 或者他们会使用承包了其他合法拆迁工作的挖掘机。

sentences.en: They would drive them over in the night, knock down an abandoned house, and then return later to steal the bricks.
sentences.zh: 他们会在夜里把挖掘机开过来，推倒一栋废弃房屋，然后再回来偷砖。

sentences.en: One of the more drastic methods of stealing bricks involves burning the buildings firSt.
sentences.zh: 最极端的偷砖方法之一是先放火烧毁建筑。

sentences.en: The fire destroys the wooden supports holding up the building and weakens the mortar between the bricks.
sentences.zh: 火灾会摧毁支撑建筑的木质结构，并削弱砖块之间的砂浆。

sentences.en: When the fire department would arrive to put out the fire, their high pressure hoses often knock down the walls and even clean the mortar off the bricks.
sentences.zh: 当消防队赶来灭火时，他们的高压水枪往往会冲垮墙壁，甚至把砖块上的砂浆冲洗干净。

sentences.en: Michael Allen is a preservationist who used to live in North St. Louis back in 2008 when brick theft was at its worst and dozens of buildings were being stolen each month.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·艾伦是一位文物保护主义者，2008年砖块盗窃最猖獗、每月有几十栋建筑被偷时，他曾住在北圣路易斯。

sentences.en: I personally worked with some neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我亲自和一些邻居合作过。

sentences.en: We boarded up buildings that weren't boarded because we weren't waiting for the city.
sentences.zh: 我们把那些没封上的建筑钉死，因为我们不想等政府处理。

sentences.en: We nailed shut the doors to keep people out of them from setting the fires inside.
sentences.zh: 我们钉死了门，防止人们进去纵火。

sentences.en: And then, you know, they'd be on fire.
sentences.zh: 结果你知道，它们还是着火了。

sentences.en: It just didn't seem real.
sentences.zh: 这简直让人难以置信。

sentences.en: Driving home to go get groceries past, like, these buildings that had been stolen seemed otherworldly.
sentences.zh: 开车回家买菜时经过这些被偷走的建筑，感觉就像在另一个世界。

sentences.en: Stealing the buildings is back-breaking work, and it can be dangerous.
sentences.zh: 偷建筑是极其耗费体力的工作，而且很危险。

sentences.en: And a couple times we have found people upside down in the rubble that got caught.
sentences.zh: 我们有几次发现有人被倒塌的瓦砾压住，头朝下困在里面。

sentences.en: The bricks caught them and killed them.
sentences.zh: 砖块压住了他们，导致他们丧命。

sentences.en: Eventually, Alderman Moore got fed up with sitting in his car and watching all this happen to his neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 最终，摩尔议员厌倦了坐在车里看着这一切发生在自己的社区。

sentences.en: So he started to confront the thieves when he would find them.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始在发现小偷时与他们对峙。

sentences.en: People have been warning me, man, Sam, they got guns.
sentences.zh: 人们一直警告我，嘿，萨姆，他们有枪。

sentences.en: They don't like you.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢你。

sentences.en: You need to stop running up on people.
sentences.zh: 你得停止冲上去找他们麻烦。

sentences.en: So I took his advice.
sentences.zh: 所以我听了他的建议。

sentences.en: I stopped running up on them.
sentences.zh: 我不再冲上去找他们了。

sentences.en: Moore eventually realized his interventions weren't making much of a difference anyway.
sentences.zh: 摩尔最终意识到，他的干预并没有起到多大作用。

sentences.en: Brick theft is classified as a nuisance crime, kind of like breaking windows in an old building.
sentences.zh: 偷砖被归类为妨害治安罪，就像打破旧建筑的窗户一样。

sentences.en: It carries a maximum $500 fine and up to 90 days in jail.
sentences.zh: 最高罚款500美元，最高可判处90天监禁。

sentences.en: And given the amount of money that can be made selling stolen brick, a lot of people figure it's a risk worth taking.
sentences.zh: 考虑到倒卖偷来的砖块能赚不少钱，很多人觉得这风险值得一冒。

sentences.en: To me, what makes used brick so special and desirable is the color.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，旧砖之所以如此特别且令人向往，是因为它的颜色。

sentences.en: This is Barbara Buck.
sentences.zh: 这位是芭芭拉·巴克。

sentences.en: She owns Century Used Brick.
sentences.zh: 她拥有“世纪旧砖”公司。

sentences.en: It's a brickyard in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 这是圣路易斯的一家砖场。

sentences.en: And so when they tear the building down, you'll get like this mix of colors of oranges and reds.
sentences.zh: 当他们拆除建筑时，你会得到这种橙色和红色的混合色。

sentences.en: And it's really hard.
sentences.zh: 而且它非常坚硬。

sentences.en: It's been really hard for new brick manufacturers to duplicate that.
sentences.zh: 新砖制造商很难复制这种效果。

sentences.en: Buck says her brickyard is scrupulous about only buying legally salvaged brick.
sentences.zh: 巴克说，她的砖场非常谨慎，只购买合法回收的砖块。

sentences.en: They typically buy from just a handful of trusted vendors.
sentences.zh: 他们通常只从少数几家值得信赖的供应商那里采购。

sentences.en: Because we're legal, we have to know exactly where our brick comes from.
sentences.zh: 因为我们是合法的，我们必须确切知道砖块的来源。

sentences.en: So we don't usually have people showing up at our yard with just a pallet, you know, trying to sell a pallet.
sentences.zh: 所以通常不会有人直接带着一托盘砖到我们场子里来兜售。

sentences.en: But Buck says there are other brick buyers that aren't as careful as she is.
sentences.zh: 但巴克说，还有其他砖块买家不像她这么谨慎。

sentences.en: There was a guy in St. Louis that people were, he was buying brick, you know, after hours, one in the morning.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯有个家伙，人们……他会在下班后，凌晨一点买砖。

sentences.en: You could get a shopping cart, fill it full of brick, go get money and go buy your drugs.
sentences.zh: 你可以推个购物车，装满砖块，换点钱去买毒品。

sentences.en: And he was doing a huge business.
sentences.zh: 他的生意做得很大。

sentences.en: And then the police shut him down.
sentences.zh: 后来警察把他查封了。

sentences.en: Buck explained to me that the supply of legally salvaged bricks is driven mostly by city-funded demolitions.
sentences.zh: 巴克向我解释说，合法回收砖块的供应主要由政府资助的拆迁工程驱动。

sentences.en: So when the city runs out of money to tear down old buildings,
sentences.zh: 所以当政府没钱拆除旧建筑时，

sentences.en: more brickyards are willing to turn a blind eye to brick acquired illegally.
sentences.zh: 更多的砖场愿意对非法获取的砖块睁一只眼闭一只眼。

sentences.en: And so that's when it gets, you know, tempting to, for these guys to steal brick and sell it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么这些人会觉得偷砖卖砖很有诱惑力。

sentences.en: Because they know there's a lot of demand and no supply.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道需求很大，而供应不足。

sentences.en: Some of the brick, whether it's legally salvaged or not, goes to building or renovating new homes in St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 无论是否合法回收，一些砖块会被用于圣路易斯的新房建设或翻新。

sentences.en: But most of it heads to another part of the country entirely.
sentences.zh: 但大部分砖块都流向了全国的其他地区。

sentences.en: I would say most of it goes to Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 我想大部分都去了路易斯安那州。

sentences.en: And we sell some in Florida.
sentences.zh: 我们也卖一些到佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: We sell some in Mississippi.
sentences.zh: 卖一些到密西西比州。

sentences.en: We sell in Texas.
sentences.zh: 卖到德克萨斯州。

sentences.en: So there's, you know, southern markets that really love our brick.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，南方市场真的很喜欢我们的砖。

sentences.en: I'm 63 years old.
sentences.zh: 我今年63岁了。

sentences.en: I've been doing this since I was 18.
sentences.zh: 我从18岁就开始干这一行。

sentences.en: And I've seen and heard just about anything you can think of in the brick business.
sentences.zh: 在砖块生意里，你想得到的、想不到的我都见过听过。

sentences.en: Gary McConnell owns McConnell Brick in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.
sentences.zh: 加里·麦康奈尔在路易斯安那州巴吞鲁日拥有麦康奈尔砖厂。

sentences.en: And he's been buying salvaged brick for decades.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，他一直在购买回收砖。

sentences.en: When demand was at its highest, he was getting boxcars full of used brick from St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 需求最高的时候，他能收到整整几车皮从圣路易斯运来的旧砖。

sentences.en: New brick might sell for around $350 per thousand.
sentences.zh: 新砖的售价大约是每千块350美元。

sentences.en: Old brick, on the other hand, will go for almost two times that.
sentences.zh: 而旧砖的价格几乎是新砖的两倍。

sentences.en: For example, we sell St. Louis brick for $675 a thousand.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们卖的圣路易斯砖是每千块675美元。

sentences.en: There are a few reasons why there's such a high demand for salvaged bricks in the southern United States, where McConnell's from.
sentences.zh: 在美国南部，也就是麦康奈尔所在的地区，对回收砖的需求如此之高，原因有几个。

sentences.en: For one thing, in the 1960s and 70s, as neighborhoods in St. Louis were starting to hollow out,
sentences.zh: 首先，在20世纪60年代和70年代，随着圣路易斯的社区开始空心化，

sentences.en: a new style of architecture in the South was creating a market for used brick.
sentences.zh: 南方的一种新建筑风格创造了对旧砖的市场需求。

sentences.en: We had an architect in Louisiana named A.
sentences.zh: 我们在路易斯安那州有一位建筑师叫A·海耶斯·汤恩，

sentences.en: Hayes Town, and he was the first person that I know of, and I was a kid back then,
sentences.zh: 他是我所知的第一个用回收材料设计房屋的人，那时我还是个孩子，

sentences.en: but he started designing houses using salvaged material.
sentences.zh: 但他开始设计使用回收材料的房屋。

sentences.en: Town was influenced by antebellum southern architecture.
sentences.zh: 汤恩受到了战前南方建筑的影响。

sentences.en: Of course, you know, we're down south.
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，我们在南方。

sentences.en: We have plantation homes.
sentences.zh: 我们有种植园住宅。

sentences.en: All those old, old plantation mansions and stuff, the brick were actually made on site.
sentences.zh: 所有那些古老的种植园豪宅之类的，砖块其实都是现场制作的。

sentences.en: By enslaved workers living on the plantation.
sentences.zh: 由住在种植园的奴隶劳工制作。

sentences.en: And they would make the brick and put them on these houses.
sentences.zh: 他们制作砖块并盖在这些房子上。

sentences.en: So when Mr. Town, his reputation and his flair was to replicate some of these old plantation homes.
sentences.zh: 所以当汤恩先生的名声和才华在于复制这些古老的种植园住宅时，

sentences.en: So the only way that you could do that was to use antique brick.
sentences.zh: 唯一的方法就是使用古董砖。

sentences.en: Town's designs called for used brick, not just for the facades of homes, but for the flooring, courtyard patios, and pool decks.
sentences.zh: 汤恩的设计要求使用旧砖，不仅用于房屋外墙，还用于地板、庭院露台和泳池甲板。

sentences.en: Even today, some neighborhoods in Baton Rouge require all new construction to use reclaimed brick.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，巴吞鲁日的一些社区也要求所有新建建筑必须使用回收砖。

sentences.en: Demand for that weathered look has gotten so high that only the wealthiest homeowners can afford to have salvaged brick.
sentences.zh: 对这种风化外观的需求已经变得如此之高，以至于只有最富有的房主才买得起回收砖。

sentences.en: They're expecting to have salvaged brick or, you know, old brick floors or pine beams or pine flooring,
sentences.zh: 他们期待拥有回收砖，或者你知道，旧砖地板、松木梁或松木地板，

sentences.en: any kind of antique salvaged stuff.
sentences.zh: 任何种类的古董回收材料。

sentences.en: They're expecting to see that in those upper-end houses.
sentences.zh: 他们期待在那些高端住宅中看到这些。

sentences.en: Aside from this desire for an antique look,
sentences.zh: 除了对古董外观的渴望之外，

sentences.en: there's another reason why so much used brick from St. Louis is headed to the Gulf Coast and out weSt.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个原因导致大量圣路易斯的旧砖流向墨西哥湾沿岸和西部。

sentences.en: It's because not all bricks are created equal.
sentences.zh: 这是因为并非所有砖块都是一样的。

sentences.en: The exterior layer of brick, the face brick, produced in St. Louis,
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯生产的外层砖，即面砖，

sentences.en: is fired in such a way that it helps it withstand the freezing winters in the MidweSt.
sentences.zh: 其烧制方式有助于它抵御中西部寒冷的冬天。

sentences.en: Interior brick is softer and can't stand up to the elements.
sentences.zh: 内墙砖较软，无法抵御恶劣天气。

sentences.en: In the 1960s and 70s, St. Louis home builders in the suburbs who started using reclaimed brick from the city
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代和70年代，圣路易斯郊区的房屋建筑商开始使用从市区回收的砖块，

sentences.en: got a nasty surprise.
sentences.zh: 结果遭到了惨痛的教训。

sentences.en: The brick facades were crumbling away.
sentences.zh: 砖墙外立面正在崩塌。

sentences.en: If you're going to put used brick on a new home,
sentences.zh: 如果你要在新房上使用旧砖，

sentences.en: there has to be someone at the demolition site
sentences.zh: 拆迁现场必须有人

sentences.en: separating out the face brick from the interior brick.
sentences.zh: 把面砖和内墙砖分开。

sentences.en: That's something demolition companies can't or won't pay for.
sentences.zh: 这是拆迁公司做不到也不愿支付成本的工作。

sentences.en: The easiest thing for them to do is just ship all of the bricks down to warmer climates,
sentences.zh: 对他们来说，最简单的方法就是把所有的砖都运往气候更温暖的地区，

sentences.en: where even the softer ones can be used on the exteriors of buildings.
sentences.zh: 在那里，即使是较软的砖块也可以用在建筑外墙上。

sentences.en: To me, there's something sad about the beautiful old houses of St. Louis
sentences.zh: 对我来说，圣路易斯那些美丽的古老建筑

sentences.en: being torn down to build beautiful old looking houses somewhere else.
sentences.zh: 被拆除以在别处建造看起来很美的古老风格建筑，这让人感到悲哀。

sentences.en: Barbara Buck, who runs the St. Louis Brickyard, agrees.
sentences.zh: 经营圣路易斯砖场的芭芭拉·巴克也表示赞同。

sentences.en: You know, there are just times when I'll go to a building that I know is coming down,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时我去一栋我知道即将被拆除的建筑时，

sentences.en: and I just feel so sad because I think about the family.
sentences.zh: 我会感到非常难过，因为我会想到那个家庭。

sentences.en: You know, I'm very sentimental.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我非常多愁善感。

sentences.en: I think about the family that lived there.
sentences.zh: 我会想到曾经住在那里的人家。

sentences.en: I think about the family that built that house.
sentences.zh: 我会想到建造那栋房子的家庭。

sentences.en: I think about the generations that were raised in that house.
sentences.zh: 我会想到在那栋房子里长大的几代人。

sentences.en: But she's also practical.
sentences.zh: 但她也很务实。

sentences.en: Many houses can't and maybe shouldn't be saved.
sentences.zh: 许多房子无法，或许也不应该被保留。

sentences.en: We don't have the population.
sentences.zh: 我们没有足够的人口。

sentences.en: We don't have the jobs to support those houses, and everything has a lifespan.
sentences.zh: 我们没有足够的工作岗位来支撑这些房子，而且万物皆有寿命。

sentences.en: The worst of the brick theft is over today.
sentences.zh: 今天，最严重的偷砖现象已经结束了。

sentences.en: Some of the brickyards that had a history of buying stolen bricks
sentences.zh: 一些有购买被盗砖块历史的砖场

sentences.en: were shut down with the help of city workers, local activists, and representatives,
sentences.zh: 在政府工作人员、当地活动家和代表的帮助下被关闭了，

sentences.en: like Alderman Sam Moore.
sentences.zh: 比如萨姆·摩尔议员。

sentences.en: Brickyards in St. Louis are now required to photograph whoever sells them brick,
sentences.zh: 现在圣路易斯的砖场被要求拍摄任何向他们出售砖块的人，

sentences.en: along with the demolition permit for that job.
sentences.zh: 并提供该工程的拆迁许可证。

sentences.en: Now, the question is how to reinvent what's left behind.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是如何重塑留下的空地。

sentences.en: Back in the Ville, Moore shows me some of the things they're doing with the vacant lots in the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 回到维尔区，摩尔向我展示了他们正在利用社区空地做的一些事情。

sentences.en: We pull up next to a fence decorated with life-size portraits of old Negro League baseball players from the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 我们停在了一道围栏旁，上面装饰着20世纪30年代黑人联盟棒球运动员的真人大小肖像。

sentences.en: Behind the fence is one of Moore's projects, an urban farm.
sentences.zh: 围栏后面是摩尔的项目之一，一个城市农场。

sentences.en: This is called the Ville Archer.
sentences.zh: 这叫“维尔拱门”。

sentences.en: We've got about 50 fruit trees in it.
sentences.zh: 我们种了大约50棵果树。

sentences.en: We're growing tilapia fish.
sentences.zh: 我们还在养罗非鱼。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: And catfish.
sentences.zh: 还有鲶鱼。

sentences.en: We've got a hatchery in there.
sentences.zh: 我们在里面有个孵化场。

sentences.en: We've got chickens.
sentences.zh: 我们有鸡。

sentences.en: We've got the works.
sentences.zh: 我们什么都有。

sentences.en: And there's new housing being built in the Ville, too.
sentences.zh: 维尔区也在建造新的住房。

sentences.en: But not the same kind of stately homes that the neighborhood used to be known for.
sentences.zh: 但不再是这个社区过去闻名的那种庄严的住宅了。

sentences.en: It'd take a million dollars to build them old houses over again.
sentences.zh: 重建那些老房子得花上一百万美元。

sentences.en: So, we want mixed use in there.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们想在那儿搞混合用途开发。

sentences.en: I think they look good.
sentences.zh: 我觉得它们看起来不错。

sentences.en: Anything to enhance the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 任何能改善社区环境的事物都好。

sentences.en: Moore shows me some of the new houses.
sentences.zh: 摩尔带我看了看一些新房子。

sentences.en: A traditional brick home in this neighborhood would have been made with walls that were three bricks deep.
sentences.zh: 在这个社区，传统的砖房墙体通常有三层砖那么厚。

sentences.en: From the street, the new houses look kind of like the old ones,
sentences.zh: 从街上看，这些新房子看起来和老房子有点像，

sentences.en: but up close you can see that there's something different.
sentences.zh: 但近看你就会发现有些不同。

sentences.en: It's not a whole brick.
sentences.zh: 那不是一整块砖。

sentences.en: Those are little clip-on gadgets.
sentences.zh: 那些是小巧的卡扣式装饰件。

sentences.en: It's a flat surface.
sentences.zh: 表面是平的。

sentences.en: It's about three-quarters of an inch thick.
sentences.zh: 厚度大约只有四分之三英寸。

sentences.en: It's a veneer of a brick.
sentences.zh: 那是砖贴面。

sentences.en: The clip-on brick works just like siding on a house.
sentences.zh: 这种卡扣式砖块的作用就像房屋的壁板一样。

sentences.en: It's a slice of used or manufactured brick attached to the wooden frame of the building
sentences.zh: 它是一片旧砖或人造砖，安装在建筑的木框架上，

sentences.en: to give it that look of a brick home.
sentences.zh: 为了让它看起来像砖房。

sentences.en: These homes, with their brick veneer, are far cheaper to build
sentences.zh: 这些带有砖贴面的房子建造起来要便宜得多，

sentences.en: and will likely be the new face of the Ville.
sentences.zh: 很可能会成为维尔社区的新面貌。

sentences.en: They're not as ornate as the old turn-of-the-century houses that used to define this neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 它们不像世纪之交时定义了这个社区的老房子那样华丽。

sentences.en: But their affordability gets more people to move in, to lower the vacancy rate.
sentences.zh: 但它们的经济适用性吸引了更多人搬进来，从而降低了空置率。

sentences.en: And that's what counts.
sentences.zh: 而这才是最重要的。

sentences.en: Better to have a neighborhood full of life, even if the brick is fake,
sentences.zh: 即便砖是假的，拥有一个充满活力的社区也更好，

sentences.en: and replace those dollhouses with real houses.
sentences.zh: 总比那些“玩具屋”强，我们要的是真正的房子。

sentences.en: A lot of cities were ravaged by fire in the mid-19th century.
sentences.zh: 19世纪中期，许多城市都遭受了火灾的蹂躏。

sentences.en: St. Louis reacted by building everything with brick.
sentences.zh: 圣路易斯对此的反应是全部用砖块建造。

sentences.en: But when San Francisco burned down, it used brick in another novel way.
sentences.zh: 但当旧金山被烧毁时，它以另一种新颖的方式使用了砖块。

sentences.en: We have a cool extra story about that after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们还有一个关于此事的精彩番外故事。

sentences.en: So a lot of other cities were also hit by fires in the mid-1800s, just like St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 所以，和圣路易斯一样，许多其他城市在19世纪中期也遭遇了火灾。

sentences.en: The 19th century was a very dangerous time in San Francisco, for example, in regards to fire.
sentences.zh: 例如，19世纪的旧金山是一个非常危险的时期，尤其是在火灾方面。

sentences.en: People who came out for the gold rush lived wherever they could,
sentences.zh: 淘金热时期来到这里的人们住在任何能住的地方，

sentences.en: in wood shacks and tents and even on wooden boats in the shallows of the bay.
sentences.zh: 木棚、帐篷，甚至海湾浅滩上的木船里。

sentences.en: It was a disaster waiting to happen.
sentences.zh: 那简直是一场随时可能发生的灾难。

sentences.en: And Kurt Kohlstedt is here in the studio with me now
sentences.zh: 现在库尔特·科尔斯特德就在演播室和我一起，

sentences.en: to talk about how fire shaped San Francisco's architecture and infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 来谈谈火灾是如何塑造旧金山的建筑和基础设施的。

sentences.en: In 1849, the same year that St. Louis suffered from a severe fire
sentences.zh: 1849年，也就是圣路易斯遭受严重火灾的那一年，

sentences.en: that ultimately turned them toward fireproof brick,
sentences.zh: 那场火灾最终促使他们转向了防火砖结构，

sentences.en: San Francisco was also hit by the first of a series of seven fires.
sentences.zh: 旧金山也遭遇了七场系列火灾中的第一场。

sentences.en: And two years later, one of these destroyed an estimated 2,000 buildings,
sentences.zh: 两年后，其中一场火灾摧毁了估计约2000座建筑，

sentences.en: amounting to about three quarters of the city at the time.
sentences.zh: 相当于当时整个城市四分之三的规模。

sentences.en: And just so you know, the reason why there's a phoenix on the flag of San Francisco
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，旧金山市旗上之所以有一只凤凰，

sentences.en: is because of all these fires of the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 就是因为19世纪50年代发生的这些火灾。

sentences.en: Just a little fun fact.
sentences.zh: 一个小趣闻。

sentences.en: But one of the things that's very clear is that San Francisco did not go the route of St. Louis.
sentences.zh: 但有一点很明确，旧金山并没有走圣路易斯那条路。

sentences.en: There are not a lot of brick buildings in response to the fires of the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 为了应对19世纪50年代的火灾，这里并没有建造大量的砖砌建筑。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So brick was expensive out in the bay and the climate doesn't really require the insulation
sentences.zh: 因为在海湾地区砖块很贵，而且气候并不真正需要那种隔热效果，

sentences.en: or benefit from the thermal mass that brick provides.
sentences.zh: 也无法从砖块提供的热质量中获益。

sentences.en: So a lot of the city was actually rebuilt using wood.
sentences.zh: 所以这座城市大部分实际上是重建时使用了木材。

sentences.en: But they did widen city streets to slow the spread of flames
sentences.zh: 但他们确实拓宽了城市街道以减缓火势蔓延，

sentences.en: and they funded better equipped firefighting forces.
sentences.zh: 并资助了装备更精良的消防力量。

sentences.en: The city even imposed a range of fines for any citizen who stood by
sentences.zh: 市政府甚至对任何袖手旁观、

sentences.en: and didn't help to put out future fires.
sentences.zh: 不帮忙扑灭未来火灾的市民处以罚款。

sentences.en: So they basically conscripted regular citizens to be involuntary firefighters?
sentences.zh: 所以他们基本上是强征普通市民成为非自愿的消防员？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't know if that would fly today.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这在今天还能不能行得通。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不行。

sentences.en: But, and these fires, they also led to this creation of this underground cistern system around the city
sentences.zh: 但是，这些火灾也促成了城市周围地下蓄水池系统的建立，

sentences.en: which provided water reserves for firefighters so they could tap the water closer to a blaze.
sentences.zh: 这为消防员提供了储备水源，让他们可以在离火场更近的地方取水。

sentences.en: But the importance of these wouldn't actually be realized until about a half century later.
sentences.zh: 但这些设施的重要性直到半个世纪后才真正显现出来。

sentences.en: You mean for the big San Francisco earthquake of 1906?
sentences.zh: 你是说1906年的旧金山大地震吗？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Water mains broke, rubble prevented firefighters from reaching parts of the city,
sentences.zh: 当时水管破裂，瓦砾阻碍了消防员到达城市的部分地区，

sentences.en: the fire ended up burning for days and thousands of lives were loSt.
sentences.zh: 火灾最终燃烧了数天，数千人丧生。

sentences.en: And most of the city was destroyed.
sentences.zh: 城市大部分地区被毁。

sentences.en: But in the aftermath, San Francisco set about expanding its auxiliary water supply system
sentences.zh: 但在那之后，旧金山着手扩建其辅助供水系统，

sentences.en: with reservoirs, pump stations, fireboats, and more earthquake-proof cisterns using concrete and steel,
sentences.zh: 增加了水库、泵站、消防船，以及更多使用混凝土和钢材建造的抗震蓄水池，

sentences.en: all which were designed to help in emergencies when conventional water systems fail.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是为了在常规供水系统失效的紧急情况下提供帮助。

sentences.en: Those all sound like very good solutions, but it doesn't sound like building with wood was a good idea still.
sentences.zh: 这些听起来都是很好的解决方案，但用木头建造听起来仍然不是个好主意。

sentences.en: Well, it was and it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，既是也不是。

sentences.en: I mean, masonry is better for fires, but it's not as great in earthquakes.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，砖石结构对防火更好，但在地震中表现就不那么出色了。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But all that being said, bricks did have a role to play.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，砖块确实发挥了一定的作用。

sentences.en: Walking around the city today, you can spot where the city cisterns are
sentences.zh: 今天走在城市里，你可以发现城市蓄水池的位置，

sentences.en: because they're marked out on the surface with big circles of bricks on San Francisco streets.
sentences.zh: 因为它们在旧金山的街道表面用巨大的砖圈标记了出来。

sentences.en: So the bricks aren't actually part of the cistern, but they do indicate where the cistern is.
sentences.zh: 所以这些砖块实际上并不是蓄水池的一部分，但它们标示了蓄水池的位置。

sentences.en: And visitors and new residents always ask about these.
sentences.zh: 游客和新居民总是会问起这些。

sentences.en: They're a huge mystery.
sentences.zh: 它们是一个巨大的谜团。

sentences.en: What are those circle outlines that they're almost as big as a city street, actually?
sentences.zh: 那些圆形的轮廓是什么？它们实际上几乎和城市街道一样大。

sentences.en: Yeah, they stretch basically from sidewalk to sidewalk, and they hint at something much larger below.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们基本上从人行道延伸到人行道，暗示着下方有更宏大的东西。

sentences.en: Ultimately, they aid visibility, making these cisterns easier to spot in a crisis.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，它们有助于提高可见度，使这些蓄水池在危机时刻更容易被发现。

sentences.en: And the middle of these brick circles are these little manhole covers that provide the actual access to the cistern.
sentences.zh: 在这些砖圈的中间是小小的井盖，提供了进入蓄水池的实际通道。

sentences.en: And being spread around the city, these mini-reservoirs can function independently if quake damage cuts off one area from another.
sentences.zh: 由于分布在城市各处，这些小型水库可以独立运作，以防地震破坏导致一个区域与另一个区域隔绝。

sentences.en: And in total, there are about 170 of these spread around, and they have a combined capacity of around 10 million gallons.
sentences.zh: 总共有大约170个这样的蓄水池分布在各处，总容量约为1000万加仑。

sentences.en: That's amazing.
sentences.zh: 太惊人了。

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And so if you're walking through San Francisco, you should really look for them because they're quite cool.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你在旧金山散步，真的应该留意一下，因为它们非常酷。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I actually wrote an article titled Decoding Rings on our website, which talks more about the history, has images and videos, but most importantly, it has a map.
sentences.zh: 我实际上在我们的网站上写了一篇题为《解码圆环》的文章，里面谈到了更多历史，有图片和视频，但最重要的是，它有一张地图。

sentences.en: So you can actually hunt these down yourself if you want to.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你愿意，实际上可以自己去寻找它们。

sentences.en: Oh, nice.
sentences.zh: 哦，不错。

sentences.en: And that website is?
sentences.zh: 那个网站是？

sentences.en: 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 99pi.org.

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible was produced this week by Zach Dyer, edited by Delaney Hall, mix and tech production by Sharif Youssef, music by Sean Rial.
sentences.zh: 本周的《99% Invisible》由扎克·戴尔制作，德莱尼·霍尔编辑，谢里夫·优素福负责混音和技术制作，肖恩·里亚尔配乐。

sentences.en: Katie Mingle is our senior producer.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂·明格尔是我们的资深制作人。

sentences.en: Kurt Kolstad is the digital director.
sentences.zh: 库尔特·科尔斯特德是数字总监。

sentences.en: Rounding out the team is Avery Truffleman, Emmett Fitzgerald, Taryn Mazza, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 团队成员还包括艾弗里·特鲁夫曼、埃米特·菲茨杰拉德、塔琳·马扎，以及我，罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7KALW in San Francisco and produced on Radio Row in beautiful downtown Oakland, California.
sentences.zh: 我们是旧金山91.7 KALW的一个项目，在加利福尼亚州奥克兰市美丽的广播街制作。

sentences.en: 99% Invisible is a member of Radiotopia from PRX, an independent collective of the most innovative shows in all of podcasting.
sentences.zh: 《99% Invisible》是PRX旗下Radiotopia的成员，这是一个由播客界最具创新性的节目组成的独立集体。

sentences.en: Find them all at radiotopia.fm.
sentences.zh: 请在radiotopia.fm上找到它们。

sentences.en: We are supported by the Knight Foundation and listener donors who pitch in whatever they can to keep us honest and keep us working hard.
sentences.zh: 我们得到了奈特基金会和听众捐赠者的支持，他们尽其所能地捐款，让我们保持客观并继续努力工作。

sentences.en: You can find the show and join discussions about the show on Facebook.
sentences.zh: 你可以在Facebook上找到我们的节目并参与讨论。

sentences.en: You can tweet at me, at Roman Mars, and the show at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 你可以在推特上艾特我@Roman Mars，或者艾特节目@99pi.org。

sentences.en: We're on Instagram, Tumblr, and Reddit, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也在Instagram、Tumblr和Reddit上。

sentences.en: But if you're thinking, I need more 99pi in my life, well, we have all the old episodes available and new articles about design every couple of days on our beautiful website.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在想，我的生活需要更多《99pi》，好吧，我们所有的旧剧集都可以在我们美丽的网站上找到，而且每隔几天就会有关于设计的新文章。

sentences.en: It's at 99pi.org.
sentences.zh: 网址是99pi.org。
